themes_detail.label: Street Vendor Crackdown Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK, a 2300% spike versus the 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69), suggesting either a sudden enforcement blitz or emerging vendor conflict in Central Harlem.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme deviation
No prior reporting or community board agenda items addressing vendor issues
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors in Central Harlem about recent enforcement actions—are they facing new restrictions, fines, or relocations?
Contact NYPD and Department of Consumer Affairs to determine if there was a coordinated enforcement operation this week

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Vandalism Wave
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK, representing a 1020% increase from the 0.6 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.74), signaling a possible coordinated tagging campaign or deteriorating maintenance response.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (1020% spike)
Z-score of 5.74 shows statistically significant anomaly
Community board repeatedly budgets for Parks maintenance, suggesting chronic resource constraints
reporting_angles: Map the 7 complaints geographically—are they concentrated in one neighborhood block or dispersed across CD 110?
Interview Parks Department about graffiti removal capacity and response times; cross-reference budget requests for maintenance equipment

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street Condition complaints jumped to 27 THIS WEEK, a 391% increase versus the 5.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 4.97), pointing to accelerating pothole, pavement, or roadway failures in Central Harlem.
evidence: 27 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.5 weekly baseline (391% spike)
Z-score of 4.97 indicates statistically significant deterioration event
Community board chronically requests Parks and DOE capital funding, suggesting deferred maintenance across district
445 DOB filings including 376 alterations and 9 demolitions may be straining street infrastructure
reporting_angles: Conduct street survey in Central Harlem—photograph and map pothole density to quantify visible decay
Interview Department of Transportation about repair backlog and timeline for addressing the spike; ask about resource allocation to CD 110

themes_detail.label: Water Conservation Alerts
themes_detail.summary: Water Conservation complaints spiked to 5 LAST WEEK, a 400% increase from the 1.0 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 4.62), potentially indicating a water main break, system failure, or city-mandated conservation campaign affecting Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 water conservation complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (400% spike)
Z-score of 4.62 shows statistically anomalous pattern
Heat/Hot Water remains the district's highest complaint category at 8026 complaints over 90 days, suggesting pre-existing water system stress
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to learn if a water main break, main line repair, or citywide conservation directive occurred last week in or near CD 110
Cross-reference with Heat/Hot Water complaints to see if the spike correlates with boiler or building-level water system failures

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food Establishment complaints jumped to 10 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 248% increase from the 2.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 4.04), suggesting either a foodborne illness cluster or heightened inspection activity at restaurants in Central Harlem.
evidence: 10 food establishment complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.9 weekly baseline (248% spike)
Z-score of 4.04 indicates statistically significant cluster
No corresponding Reddit discussion or news coverage suggests the issue may be under-reported
reporting_angles: Request DOH inspection data for Central Harlem restaurants 2 weeks ago—did multiple establishments fail health inspections or report violations?
Interview restaurant owners and health department to determine if the spike reflects a targeted enforcement campaign or actual health code violations
